title: Verb To Be & Introductions
objectives: Use am, is, and are correctly with subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they).
Introduce yourself with your name, nationality, and job or role.
Ask and answer simple questions about personal information.
Form basic affirmative, negative, and question sentences with the verb to be.
canDo: I can introduce myself and talk about basic personal information using the verb to be.

warmUp.title: Think before you start
warmUp.prompt: How do you introduce yourself in Portuguese? Try to say your name, where you are from, and what you do — now imagine saying the same things in English. In this lesson you will learn the most important verb in English: to be (ser / estar).

explanation:
The verb to be is essential in English. We use it to say who we are, where we are from, our job, our age, and how we feel. In Portuguese you have two verbs (ser and estar), but in English there is one verb with three forms in the present: am, is, and are.

Key pattern:
• I am (I'm)
• You / We / They are (You're / We're / They're)
• He / She / It is (He's / She's / It's)

Common introduction phrases:
• Hello! / Hi!
• My name is… / I'm…
• I am from…
• I am a student / teacher / engineer.
• Nice to meet you!

To ask about someone:
• What is your name?
• Where are you from?
• Are you a student?

Short answers: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. / Yes, she is. / No, he isn't.

grammar.title: The Verb To Be — Present Simple
grammar.rule: Use am with I; is with he, she, it; and are with you, we, they. Add not for negatives (I am not, she isn't, they aren't). In questions, put am/is/are before the subject.

examples.sentence: I am Gabriel. I am from Brazil.
She is a teacher. She is not a doctor.
Are you a student? — Yes, I am.

vocabulary.example: I am a student of English.
We are happy to meet you.

reading.title: Meeting New Friends
reading.text:
Hello! My name is Julia. I am 26 years old. I am from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. I am a student of English. I am happy today because I am at an English class.

This is my classmate, Ken. He is from Tokyo, Japan. He is 27 years old. He is not a student — he is a software engineer. Ken and I are friends. We are not from the same country, but we are in the same class.

Our teacher is Ms. Clark. She is from London. She is a very nice teacher. Today she asks us: "Are you ready?" We say: "Yes, we are!"

writing.prompt: Write a short introduction about yourself (4–6 sentences). Include: your name, your nationality or city, your job or role (student, teacher, etc.), and one sentence about how you feel today. Use am, is, or are at least four times.
rubricHints: Start with a greeting: Hello! or Hi!
Use My name is… or I'm…
Use I am from… for your city or country.
Check am/is/are: I am, he/she is, we/they are.
End with Nice to meet you! or a similar closing phrase.
writing.modelAnswer: Hello! My name is Gabriel. I am from Brazil. I am a student of English. I am 30 years old. I am happy today because I am learning something new. Nice to meet you!

tutorHints: This is the learner's first lesson. Keep explanations simple and use Portuguese support only when needed for clarity.
Common errors: I is…, She are…, and translating age as 'I have X years'. Remind them: I am X years old.
Encourage full introductions: name + origin + role. Model short dialogues if they ask for speaking practice.
If they confuse ser/estar from Portuguese, explain that English to be covers both in basic introductions.
Link mistakes back to rule a1-verb-to-be and suggest review items from this lesson.
